newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia's presidency to meet in Serb territory.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia's presidency to meet in Serb territory.

text.p: Bosnia's newly-elected three-man presidency is to have its second meeting on Friday, but this time in Serb-held territory near Sarajevo.

In a breakthrough meeting on Tuesday, the Serb member of the body, Momcilo Krajisnik, ended his boycott of presidency sessions after a compromise was reached to meet alternately in different territories.
He also signed an oath of loyalty to Bosnian statehood, effectively renouncing Serb war aims for a separate state and opening the way for regular work of the presidency.

The three presidency members, a Moslem, Serb and Croat are expected to discuss the work of Bosnia's joint institutions in a Serb suburb of Lukavica and to discuss candidates for the council of ministers to govern the country.
The international community's representative in Bosnia, Carl Bildt met separately with the three national leaders on Thursday in preparation for Friday's session.
Krajisnik said after the meeting with Bildt: "We have agreed on most issues and we have cleared out problems that could occur at tomorrow's meeting."
The issue of candidates for Bosnia's central bank will be on the agenda as well, he told Bosnian Serb television.
